title: Qi Jiguang
summary: Qi Jiguang was a Ming general from a military family in Shandong. In 1556 he was appointed to defend the Zhejiang coast against Japanese pirates, and in 1557 his plan to train volunteers was approved, with three thousand men trained. He relieved Fujian in 1562, and by 1567 he and his forces had cleared the Fujian coast. He wrote the Jixiao Xinshu in 1560.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com gives only the years 1528-1588; other sources vary by a year, but none was cited.

where.modern_name: Shandong province, China (region centre; labelled proxy pin)
where.historical_name: Shandong, Ming empire (home region of his military family)

importance.justification: Defeated the wokou raids on the Ming southeast coast and shaped the northern frontier defence, including the Great Wall towers.
